en.title: Five Relations Between Circles on a Common Axis
en.description:
The centers of two circles both lie on the X axis or both lie on the Y axis (never both axes at once); classify their relation. Concentric takes priority; otherwise, one intersection point is Touching, two are Intersecting, lying apart outside each other is Disjoint-Outside, and one lying inside the other without intersecting is Disjoint-Inside. A radius of 0 is valid.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n lines of six integers x y R x2 y2 R2. 1≤n≤5000, coordinates and radii are 0..5000, and the common axis is guaranteed.
en.output: Output one English relation name per line.
en.explanation: The examples give Concentric; Touching/Intersecting; and Disjoint-Outside/Disjoint-Inside respectively.
hints: First check whether the centers are equal; otherwise compare the squared distance between the centers with the square of the sum of the radii and the square of their difference.
